summary: Observation of a luminous circle in the sky.
description: witness reported in June 2011 an observation made on December 30, 2002: while watching fireworks, he noticed an unexplained luminous phenomenon in the sky; he saw a stationary white circle of light rotating first in one direction and then in the other. Only one witness account of this phenomenon was collected. The case, reported recently (June 8, 2011), cannot be investigated. No other witness account can be corroborated with this one. The case is therefore classified as C due to a lack of information.

summary: A private pilot observed a large light coming from his direction, which then suddenly disappeared.
description: On December 9, 2002, a private pilot instructor and two student pilots saw a large light moving towards them during takeoff. The light then went out, revealing a spherical shape that abruptly changed direction. Air traffic control and radar detected nothing. Unexplained, Class D phenomenon.

summary: Observation of 2 luminous points of elongated shape moving in a straight line without any noise: passage of the ISS.
description: On December 3, 2002, at 6:00 PM, two witnesses observed two elongated, luminous points in the sky moving in a straight line without any noise. The observation lasted approximately 5 minutes. The two luminous points observed by the witnesses correspond to the International Space Station (ISS) (object 25544), which was preceded shortly by the Space Shuttle STS-113, which had undocked from the station the previous day before returning to Earth on December 7. (See the appendix for the traces of these objects recorded on the ground between 5:55 PM and 6:05 PM). This case is classified as "A" as a fully identified phenomenon.

summary: Observation by a witness of a flash resembling a rocket that moved at high speed: lack of information.
description: On November 16, 2002, at approximately 9:00 PM, a witness observed a flash resembling a rocket moving at high speed. The apparition lasted about two seconds. Class C case due to lack of information.

summary: Likely sighting of an advertising laser projector
description: On November 8, 2002, between 11:45 PM and 12:15 AM, a couple observed a luminous phenomenon consisting of about a dozen points of light arranged in an oval and rotating clockwise. At the center of the phenomenon were about half a dozen stationary points of light. No sound was heard. Although the investigation could not confirm it, it is likely, based on their description, that the witnesses saw the effects of a laser advertising projector from a great distance.

summary: A witness observed a fire-colored ball with several flashing lights.
description: On November 1, 2002, at approximately 10:00 PM, a witness observed a fire-colored sphere with several flashing lights. This sphere moved back and forth several times. The phenomenon disappeared after about 30 seconds. This observation also appears to have been made by pilots. Unexplained phenomenon, Class D.

summary: Observation of a triangular-shaped object with lights at its vertices
description: On October 29, 2002, at approximately 7:00 PM, a witness observed a triangular object with apparent dimensions of 40 to 50 cm, with lights at its apexes, moving at a constant speed along a straight trajectory without making any noise. No further information could be gathered regarding this Class C report.

summary: Observation with the naked eye and binoculars of the silent SSW-NNE movement of a group of dark objects (7 to 9) animated by movements (rotation, distancing, approaching) relative to each other as well as of a separate identical object: observations of playful balloons.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named ANNECY-LE-VIEUX (74) 20.10.2002, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On October 20, 2002, at approximately 6:40 PM, a couple observed from a terrace the silent movements of a group of 7 to 9 very small, dark or black objects in the sky. These objects exhibited different movements relative to one another. Observation with the naked eye and then with binoculars lasted approximately ten minutes. The entire group moved in a NNE direction at a speed estimated to be very low and at a constant altitude. Only one witness account was collected. Air traffic control in the area was contacted, but no unusual activity was reported. We explored two possible explanations for the phenomenon observed by the witnesses (see the investigation report). The first involves confusion with a group of blackbirds flying at high altitude in a migratory corridor. Although the geographical and temporal situation of the witnesses, located in a migratory corridor and making their observation at the end of October, in the midst of migration, supports this hypothesis, it remains nonetheless fragile, particularly for two reasons: - the known and calculated data (altitude of the unidentified flying objects/duration of observation/speed) do not match the characteristics of the birds recorded passing through that day; - and above all, the trajectory is in the opposite direction to the classic migration pattern. The second hypothesis, that of confusion with a cluster of black balloons attached by strings, fits very well with the data. A light southwest wind was blowing on the day of the observation, in the same direction as the movement of the unidentified flying objects, which was very slow. The known and calculated data relating to this speed of movement, altitude, and duration of observation fit very well with this hypothesis. Thus, with an estimated altitude of 500 m, we have a total angular displacement of approximately 67°, which is plausible given the geographical configuration of the area. Furthermore, the movements of individuals within the group (approaching, moving away, with rotations) are explained by the fact that they are connected to each other, more or less tightly, by strings. Carried by the local wind, they move as a single unit, but remain subject to small local influences causing them to move randomly and independently of one another, within the limits of the string connecting them. This playful balloon-licking variation is indeed practiced and produces such effects, as shown in this video, where the five balloons constantly change their relative position while remaining confined to a small area, all connected by strings. GEIPAN did not yet have sufficient experience with this type of balloon licking at the time of the observation and initial investigation. The observation took place on a Sunday evening in the late afternoon, which is conducive to a festive or recreational event of this kind. The consistency of the data is poor, with only one witness statement collected, even though several witnesses were present, and some data, particularly angular measurements, are missing. No photos or videos were recorded. GEIPAN classifies the case as eBe: probable observation of playful balloons.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: The crew of an A320 flying from Lisbon to Orly observed two very bright lights briefly passing over their aircraft at approximately 7:30 PM UTC on October 16, 2002, at a considerable distance estimated at over 35 km. The trajectory was rapid and descending. The observation was likely that of an atmospheric reentry, which the crew identified as such.

summary: An object falls along a 45-degree trajectory. Probable atmospheric reentry.
description: On October 8, 2002, at approximately 10:20 PM, several witnesses in different locations observed a very bright light followed by an object falling at a 45-degree angle. The phenomenon is classified as Class B and is identified as a probable atmospheric reentry.

summary: dull noise that becomes unbearable and ends with 3 violent explosions: lack of information.
description: During the night of September 21-22, 2002, around midnight, a couple was awakened by a muffled noise that became unbearable and ended with three violent explosions. The entire phenomenon lasted approximately three seconds. Curiously, their children were not awakened, and their neighbor heard nothing. No further information was available. Class C case.

summary: Observation of luminous points that appeared to fall
description: On September 2nd, at approximately 10 PM, a witness observed a series of bright lights moving from the horizon to a point where they appeared to "fall." A triangle of bright lights was also observed. No sound was heard. Class C phenomenon due to a lack of further information.

summary: Likely sighting of a weather balloon
description: On September 27, 2002 at 14:48 UTC, the crew of an A320 flying from Tenerife to Brussels observed a round object which they themselves described as a balloon, probably a weather balloon.

summary: Observation of the silent passage of a brown cylindrical object: lack of information.
description: Recent report (February 13, 2011) of an old observation without specifying the date. We arbitrarily date the observation to August 1, 2002. At the beginning of August 2002, around 8:30 PM, a motorist observed a slow-moving object in the sky, traveling in a straight line to the southeast. The object was cylindrical, brown in color, moved silently, and left a short trail behind it. He then took a photograph. The witness called the police, stating that he had seen "a rocket" traveling from northwest to southeast. It was only after finding the photograph several years later that the witness sent the questionnaire and two photographs to GEIPAN (the French National Center for Information on Astronomical Phenomena). No other reports of this phenomenon have been collected. The late date of this observation makes any investigation impossible to date.

summary: Observation by numerous witnesses of several lights moving in concert.
description: On July 5, 2002, between 10:00 PM and 10:30 PM, numerous witnesses observed several white lights aligned and moving together. The phenomenon was observed in several departments, including Vaucluse and Bouches-du-Rhône. According to the accounts, there were six or eight lights, aligned, in a circle, or in the shape of two triangles, but all agreed that the movement was uniform for all the lights. Depending on the case, the observation lasted from a few minutes to an hour. Observations in 2008 with similar characteristics were investigated and classified as A, such as the observation of a flight by the Patrouille de France: /geipan/actualites/13082009-Des-PAN-en-formation-dans-le-Vaucluse-en-Juillet-2008.html Therefore, this case was re-examined and identified as observations of the Patrouille de France.

summary: Observation of 3 vertical light bars exhibiting varied movements
description: On September 26, 2002, at approximately 3:30 a.m., a witness observed three vertical luminous bars exhibiting varying movements. The witness noted that he was "called" by "a voice" to investigate the phenomenon. No further information could be gathered regarding this Class C phenomenon.

summary: Observing the fall of an object into several pieces
description: On the night of June 2, 2002, a motorist observed an incandescent object falling and breaking into several pieces. The observation was brief (a few seconds) and made no sound. This phenomenon was classified as a probable atmospheric re-entry of space debris.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On April 6, 2002, at 10:45 PM, several independent witnesses from various departments observed the very rapid descent of a silent fireball. All witnesses indicated that the sighting occurred to the east. This phenomenon was also reported by witnesses in Bavaria. The prevailing hypothesis is that of atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observations by pilots of a brief but intense luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observations of atmospheric reentry.
description: On March 16, 2002, the crews of several aircraft reported the very rapid passage of a green light with a trail, probably originating from an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Fleeting observation of a luminous oval shape
description: On February 21, 2002, at approximately 8:00 PM, a witness out for a walk with his wife observed an oval object at high altitude. The object initially moved slowly and then disappeared with a sudden acceleration. The observation was very brief; the witness's wife saw nothing. No further information is available regarding this sighting.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On February 7, 2002, at approximately 8:00 AM, several independent witnesses observed the very rapid descent of an orange fireball. The observation was very brief (1 to 2 seconds): the fireball had a trail and disappeared quickly. Other witnesses in a neighboring department also reported observing this phenomenon, which was probably an atmospheric reentry.

summary: Observation of a luminous, saucer-shaped mass
description: On February 2, 2002, at approximately 7:40 PM, a family in a car observed a saucer-shaped illuminated object above a wooded area. In the darkness, this object, topped with a dome, was gray with spaced white lights around its edge. The phenomenon remained stationary above the trees, with witnesses estimating its diameter at about 15 meters. No unusual noises were heard. After the road changed direction, the witnesses lost sight of the object. At the time, the case was classified as a D case. Following a recent email from an internet user indicating the presence of a water tower in the observation area, which could have led to a misinterpretation at the time, the case has been reopened and further investigations are underway. Based on the witnesses' positions, it is likely that there was a misunderstanding, not with a water tower, but with the secondary radar of the General Delegation of Civil Aviation at Paris Sud Palaiseau, used for Orly Airport, which was indeed located on the line of sight and corresponds to the descriptions given by the witnesses. This case is reclassified as B.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry.
description: On January 19, 2002, at approximately 5:45 PM, a witness driving on the highway observed, for about a second, the very rapid passage of a luminous green mass across the sky with a luminous trail. This was likely an observation of atmospheric reentry.
